title: Kinley Rasmus’ Little League World Series is over, but her legacy will live on
content:
Kinley Rasmus’ portion of the 2026 Little League Baseball World Series story is now written and sealed after her Alabama team was eliminated Wednesday. Her legacy, however, will echo.

Every August, when the LLBWS record books reopen, her name will line them for what she did over the last week in Williamsport.

The 12-year-old two-way star went out fairly quietly, going 0-for-1 at the plate in her Phenix City, Ala. team’s 11-2 loss to Hamilton, Ohio, in the U.S. Elimination Bracket Semifinal. It was her team’s second loss and the end of her run.

But she displayed dominance along the way.

In five games, Rasmus took the mound twice, logging 14 strikeouts. At the plate, she powered her team’s offense, collecting five hits and three RBIs. She tied Mo’ne Davis for the most strikeouts by a girl in a tournament, and set the record for the most hits by a girl.

Just stepping into Williamsport, her name was added to an exclusive group that graced the LLBWS stage. Rasmus became the 25th girl to play in the tournament’s 79-year history and the ninth to pitch in the competition. However, her showing outclassed them all, displaying a shutdown arm commensurate to her pop at the plate.

It runs in her blood. Her father, Cory Rasmus, pitched in MLB, and her uncle, Colby, was a big-league outfielder for 10 years. Her grandfather, Tony, played in the minors but coached Cory and Colby together on the 1999 Phenix City LLBWS team that made the final against the eventual champion from Japan.

Phenix City hadn’t made it to Williamsport in the 27 years since.

Though short-lived, the bar Kinley set on both sides of the ball will live in perpetuity. When the next girl takes the mound at the LLBWS, she’ll be eyeing the strikeout record Rasmus shares with Davis. And when the next girl steps into the batter’s box, she’ll be striving for the mark that Rasmus holds alone.

History now bears the Rasmus name.

There to chase, or simply as a reminder, for years to come.
